content: Lay The Groundwork For Your Best Years
In the event of unexpected circumstances such as critical illnesses, accidents or disability, your needs and livelihood might be affected.
Protection against accidents and major illnesses so that your needs during recovery continue to be met.
Financial payout for death, terminal illness, and total and permanent disability.
Saving for and investing in your upcoming milestones are easier the earlier you start.
Savings for future expenses such as home purchase and marriage.
If you are a Singaporean or PR, you’re automatically covered by three national schemes:

MediSave
A national savings scheme which helps CPF members save for future medical expenses, especially during retirement.

MediShield Life
A health insurance for large hospital bills and selected outpatient treatment costs.

CareShield Life
Long-term care insurance scheme for financial support and monthly cash payouts in event of severe disability.
Beyond the basic coverage from national schemes, you’ll still need to ensure that you are sufficiently covered to avoid dipping into any hard-earned savings.
National schemes do not fully cover:

Hospitalisation
An Integrated Shield Plan (IP) provides additional coverage for private hospitals or higher ward classes in public hospitals.

Critical Illness
You’ll need coverage of 4x annual income. (Recommended)3

Death & Total and Permanent Disability
You’ll need coverage of 9 – 10x annual income. (Recommended)3
Make sure your insurance premiums fit comfortably within your budget. It’s recommended to spend at most 15% of take-home pay on insurance protection.
Premiums increase as you get older2.
Less likely of pre-existing conditions that could exclude you from coverage2.
Connect with a Financial Representative for personalised coverage.

Emergency Funds
At least 3 – 6 months’ worth of expenses (including dependants) for rainy days.
Savings for your upcoming expenses and a plan for you to live out your golden years comfortably – the earlier you start, the more time you have to grow your wealth and accumulate more.

Investments
It is recommended to allocate at least 10%3 of your take-home pay for key milestones.

A Retirement Plan3
It is never too early to start building your nest egg for the retirement lifestyle you want, including monthly payouts.
The earlier you start, the longer time horizon you’ll have to accumulate wealth due to the compounding effect4.
As lifespans are increasing5, you’ll need a plan for your financial needs in the future.
